title: Three pitfalls: で, が and に
summary: Three small kana each do two different jobs: で (particle or te-form of だ), が (subject marker or "but") and に (target or an old "and"). Look at what comes before and what ends the phrase.

blocks.text: Three look-alikes catch learners out. Each of **で**, **が** and **に** has one job you know and one you may not. The trick is always the same: look at what comes right before the kana.

rows: noun + で, then a verb? Place. Description + で, then more? て-form.
after a noun: subject. After a full clause: "but".
one に per item in a list of nouns
blocks.title: The three at a glance

blocks.text: As a **particle**, で follows a noun and marks where an action happens or what tool is used.
But で is also the **て-form of だ**. Compare an い-adjective: 美しい becomes 美しくて to link descriptions, and a noun or な-adjective does the same with で.

blocks.jp: さくらはかわいくて、優しい。
さくらはきれいで、優しい。

blocks.text: It links whole clauses too, and then it works like "and" or "and so".

blocks.jp: さくらはいい子で、毎日学校に行く。
blocks.en: Sakura is a good kid, and she goes to school every day.

blocks.text: The て-form of だ hides in two set phrases. お元気で works like a request (compare 待って, "please wait"). 無事でよかった means "it is good that you are safe".

As a **subject particle**, が always follows a noun. As a **connector**, が follows a complete clause (one that ends in a verb, an adjective or だ, never in a bare noun) and means "but". It is not always strongly contrastive: sometimes it only says "and then" or sets the scene.

blocks.jp: お店に行ったが、パンがなかった。
blocks.en: I went to the shop, but there was no bread.

blocks.text: A polite sentence can also end on が and leave the rest unsaid. It sounds soft and modest.

blocks.jp: コーヒーがほしいのですが……
blocks.en: I would like some coffee, but... (if it's no trouble)

blocks.text: に: target, or "and" in a list
に is the usual **target** particle. In an older, written style, it can also join items in a list, one に after each noun.

blocks.jp: 靴に指輪に帽子を買った。
blocks.en: I bought shoes, a ring and a hat.

blocks.text: The set phrase **それに** means "besides, in addition".

blocks.jp: 雨が降っている。それに、風も強い。
blocks.en: It is raining. On top of that, the wind is strong.

items: **Noun + で**: place or tool; **description + で**: て-form of だ.
**Noun + が**: subject; **complete clause + が**: but.
**に**: target; in lists, "and"; **それに**: besides.
Check what comes before the kana and how the phrase ends.

questions.note: Noun + で: means.
questions.en: I wrote my name with a pen.

questions.prompt: この部屋は静かで広い。
options: The て-form of だ, linking two descriptions
questions.note: 静か is a noun here, so the て-form of だ is で.
questions.en: This room is quiet and spacious.

questions.instruction: In which sentence is で the て-form of だ?
options: この辞書は便利で、安い。
questions.note: Predicate + で links descriptions.

questions.prompt: 今日は雨が降っているが、出かけます。
questions.note: A connector after a complete clause.
questions.en: It is raining today, but I will go out.

questions.note: が after a noun marks the subject.

questions.prompt: 弟はテニスが上手＿＿、兄は下手だ。
questions.note: A complete clause (上手だ) + が: but.
questions.en: My younger brother is good at tennis, but my older brother is bad.

questions.prompt: デパートはきれい＿＿、広いです。
questions.note: きれい (a noun) + で links descriptions.
questions.en: The department store is clean and big.

questions.prompt: 電車が遅れた＿＿、会議に間に合った。
questions.note: A complete clause + が: but.
questions.en: The train was late, but I made it to the meeting.

questions.instruction: What does the final が do?
questions.prompt: コーヒーを一杯いただきたいのですが。
questions.note: The listener fills in the rest.
questions.en: I would like a cup of coffee, if that is all right...

questions.instruction: In an old written style, what does に do in a list like this?
questions.prompt: りんごにバナナにみかんを買った。
questions.note: An old written use of に.
questions.en: I bought apples, bananas and mandarins.

questions.prompt: このレストランは安い。それに、おいしい。
questions.note: それ + に: in addition.
questions.en: This restaurant is cheap. On top of that, it is tasty.

questions.instruction: Which sentence uses が to mean "but"?
questions.note: "But" follows a full clause; the others follow a noun.

options: 雨が降っているで、行かない。
彼は医者で、毎日忙しい。
questions.note: A verb clause cannot take the て-form of だ.
Noun + に: the target.

questions.prompt: I went to the shop, but it was closed.
questions.note: Complete clause + が: but.
questions.en: I went to the shop, but it was closed.

questions.prompt: I ate dinner at a restaurant.
questions.note: Place + で.
questions.en: I ate dinner at a restaurant.

questions.prompt: This town is quiet and clean.
questions.note: The て-form of だ links descriptions.
questions.en: This town is quiet and clean.

questions.prompt: It is cold. Besides, it is raining.
questions.note: それに: on top of that.
questions.en: It is cold. Besides, it is raining.

questions.note: A complete clause + が.
questions.en: These shoes are expensive but very comfortable.

questions.instruction: Tap the word with the place particle で
questions.note: Noun + で: where it happens.
questions.en: I played with a friend in the park.

questions.instruction: Tap the word that holds the て-form of だ
questions.note: Predicate + で.

questions.instruction: Tap the word with the subject が
questions.note: Noun + が: subject.
